::: {.entry-meta}
[measurement]{.chip .measured} Entry 99 · milestone M5
:::

**The validated numerical baseline stays unchanged.** New local controls show
why choosing its radial smoothing policy needs a separate physics decision.
The [primer](../primer.qmd) explains the guarded surrogate and fallback model.

We evaluated the same retained plasma states with four radial smoothing widths.
Transition widths, guards, clipping, floors, patches and profiles stayed fixed.
The native operator includes the transport coefficients after processing, not
only the surrogate's raw particle flux.

At the particle-split boundary, smaller nonzero radii do not move the result
steadily toward the raw target: [the selected particle rate is 0%, 6.76754%, 9.05578% and 5.76626% less inward than the raw target at radial HWHM 0, 0.025, 0.05 and 0.1 respectively]{.claim}[C-312](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-312){.cid .st-measured}. The selected response to a
density perturbation also changes: [the target derivative is +39.9009; native values are +39.9009, +0.4076, −43.8378 and −38.8539 across the same widths; the +0.4076 value lacks strict finite-difference corroboration]{.claim}[C-313](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-313){.cid .st-measured}. A small AD value without
the required finite-difference agreement remains unresolved.

Zero radial width recovers the raw target at that particle state. It does not
solve every mechanism. At the coefficient-cap context, the guarded served flux
already differs before radial processing: [the selected cap rate is already 96.87350% less inward than the raw target without radial smoothing, compared with 81.44208%, 63.19414% and 65.09036% at the three nonzero widths]{.claim}[C-314](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-314){.cid .st-measured}. That raw-target
difference is not a measured physical error, and it must not be attributed
entirely to smoothing.

The saved-state reconstructions retain the original baseline control and all
derivative qualifications: [696 observations pass algebra/invariant reconstruction and 174 baseline observations reproduce the parent evidence; 996 of 1008 derivative components and 45 of 48 complete direction sets meet the strict rule]{.claim}[C-315](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-315){.cid .st-measured}. A failed cap process and a replay
checker correction remain in the evidence history; the numerical equations and
acceptance thresholds were not relaxed.

These are local operator comparisons, not five-second density or fusion-power
errors. They support a constrained particle-flux comparison through the full
postprocessing operator before any trajectory policy changes. Valid-trajectory
matched windows and an explicit density/flux accuracy requirement are still
needed to judge accumulated effects.

No production width was selected, no batch job was submitted and physicist
sign-off remains pending.
